svg.title: The two-scalar sky
svg.desc: Every prime p = 1 mod 4 up to 3000 (211 primes) placed on a Fermat sunflower spiral: the k-th prime sits at angle k times the golden angle and radius proportional to sqrt(k). Each is a glowing disc whose brightness is log(1 + N(p)) scaled to the largest value, where N(p) is the exact number of ordered two-scalar pairs (lambda, mu): lambda a nonsquare in an odd coset C_s of the odd-order subgroup H of Z_p^*, mu in lambda H, with chi((lambda - 1)(mu - 1)) = -1, (1 + mu)/(1 + lambda) in H, and (lambda mu)^(M/2) a generator of H (M = 2^v the largest power of two dividing p - 1). Each such pair is a page (two strong starters with complementary sums whose union is a Hamilton cycle) for the first-odd one-short partition of K_(p, p+2). The largest count is N(2957) = 136240. The primes with N(p) = 0 are drawn as dark holes with a thin ring and labelled; there are exactly 9: 5, 13, 17, 97, 193, 257, 577, 641, 769 (the Fermat primes 5, 17, 257 where t = 1 forces mu = lambda, and the small-t primes 13, 97, 193, 769 with t = 3, 577 with t = 9 and 641 with t = 5). Spot checks against the probe: N(41) = 4, N(73) = 20, N(89) = 16, N(113) = 12. All of this is asserted by the generating script before the picture is written.
svg.text: primes p = 1 mod 4 up to 3000 on a sunflower spiral; brightness log(1 + N(p)), N(p) = number of two-scalar pages (lambda, mu)
dark holes: the 9 primes with no two-scalar page, 5, 13, 17, 97, 193, 257, 577, 641, 769
N(p) counts ordered pairs with chi((lambda-1)(mu-1)) = -1, (1+mu)/(1+lambda) in H, (lambda mu)^(M/2) generating H; brightest: N(2957) = 136240; every count computed exactly
